messages:
maria_cheng: Quick mid-quarter check — we need to reforecast OKR progress after the infra cost spike last week. I propose we de-prioritize the ‘reranking small-latency optimization’ (was Q2 stretch) and swap in a focused cost-optimizer spike that targets token caching and a short QC for quantized models.

devon_kim: Can you share the delta on the projected burn and how that maps to the OKR %?

maria_cheng: Short summary: projected infra burn +14% vs plan for Q2 (mainly hosted serving). If we keep current scope we hit ~55% of Efficiency OKR instead of 70%. If we swap in the cost-optimizer spike we can push back to ~68%. Details:```
- baseline plan efficiency: 70%
- projected with current scope: 55%
- projected with swap: 68%
```

ashley_g: Customers (esp enterprise pilots) are already asking for better cost visibility and token cost reductions. +1 for the swap, but we need to keep a short list of acceptance criteria so we don't scope-creep.

samir_patel: Engineering note — cost-optimizer spike is doable in 3 sprints if we scope it as: lightweight prefix/KV caching improvements + autotuning of batch windows + one targeted quantization experiment (int8). If we cut the reranking micro-optimizations (some assembly kernel work), that frees ~2 dev-weeks.

jess_ops: What about launch criteria / SLO? For the OKR to count we need measurable before/after on tokens/sec and p95 latency. Can we define the metrics now?

maria_cheng: Proposed launch criteria:```
- 10-15% reduction in tokens/unit cost on hosted workloads (measured by the cost dashboard)
- no regression >5% on p95 latency for 99% of production routes
- automated canary + rollback in console for the feature flag
- documented QA prompt set and regression evals run on rollout
```

devon_kim: Sounds reasonable. One ask: mark this as a scope-change requiring EM + PM signoff (per our mid-quarter process). I'll loop in finance to rebaseline quota chargebacks.

pm-bot: Reminder: per Mid-Quarter Reforecast process, any OKR scope change requires: EM signoff, PM signoff, and updated forecast in the OKR tracker within 3 business days. Use /reforecast to generate the new forecast doc.

samir_patel: EM signoff: Samir (this thread). I agree. We’ll produce a short RFC PR for the swap-by-sprint plan by EOD tomorrow.

ashley_g: PM signoff: Ashley G (this thread). Agree, conditional on: detailed acceptance criteria + small rollback playbook.

jess_ops: Ops note — please add the new canary route to the runbook and tag oncall for the first 72h post-rollout.

maria_cheng: I'll create the OKR tracker update after RFC lands. Devon — can you chase finance? If finance flags any issues we can re-evaluate the percent to postpone.

devon_kim: On it. I’ll ping finance and drop the updated numbers into the tracker by EOD tomorrow.

samir_patel: Quick mitigation idea: if finance doesn't ok extra short-term spend, we can hybridize — run the quant experiment only on dedicated for now (no hosted change) and still count the experiment towards learning OKR but not the efficiency %. That keeps delivery velocity.

ashley_g: Fine as fallback. But prefer the hosted path if we can get the finance nod.

maria_cheng: Cool. Plan: 1) Samir to post RFC by EOD tomorrow; 2) Devon to update finance + tracker; 3) Ashley signoff + acceptance criteria confirmed; 4) Jess to update runbook. If all aligned we swap scope and update the OKR within 3 days.

pm-bot: Action items logged: samir_patel (RFC), devon_kim (finance + tracker), ashley_g (criteria), jess_ops (runbook). Deadline: 2025-03-28 17:00 UTC.

ashley_g: Thanks — will review RFC quickly once posted. :thumbsup:
